text:
The physician may be found liable if the cervical springing was performed without a documented pre-manipulation screen for cervical arterial dysfunction and vertebrobasilar insufficiency, despite red flags (age 78, severe unexplained neck pain, recent sustained overhead neck posture), and without informed consent covering stroke risk. Liability also requires expert testimony that the manipulation more likely than not caused or contributed to the posterior-circulation event, such as a vertebral artery dissection, because the four-hour timing alone does not establish causation. If the screen was done and documented, or if the event was a coincidental stroke, liability is much less likely.

CONFIDENCE: 70
